text:
maria: Hey team — ArrowHealth demo just hit a streaming failure during patient-summary generation. The UI cut off mid-JSON and the embedded Windows WebView shows a parse error. Happened ~2 minutes into the live session. Can we triage? :grimacing:
rajesh: Ugh. Do we have the raw SSE payload or request id from the demo? Which model + SDK?
maria: Model: gpt-4o-stream-v1 (hosted). SDK: web-sdk v0.9.2. Request id: req_0a9b3f. Attached console snippet from the WebView: `data: {"choices":[{"delta":{"content":"...patient has h"},"finish_reason":null}]}` then a new chunk `data: [TRUNC]` and client crashes parsing JSON.
tim: Two fast guesses: 1) proxy/nginx buffering is coalescing/truncating chunk boundaries, 2) client-side WebView hasn't handled partial UTF-8 sequences. Can we reproduce with curl against the streaming URL?
maria: I ran a curl reproduce but it kept streaming fine for me. Customer repro only on their Windows kiosk (embedded app). They use an IIS reverse-proxy in front of a company gateway.
sophie: Windows WebView (EdgeHTML/Chromium) sometimes aggressively buffers when response lacks proper Transfer-Encoding framing. Ask them to confirm response headers from the gateway.
rajesh: Also check for any intermediate middleware that rewrites Content-Length or adds gzip that might break streaming. If their gateway adds Content-Length it will buffer until full.
maria: Got headers from customer gateway: `Content-Length: 0`, `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`, and `X-Accel-Buffering: "on"` (??). They also have an app-level heartbeat turned off.
tim: Okay that explains it — X-Accel-Buffering or similar will cause buffering. Two remediation paths: 1) change gateway to disable buffering for SSE endpoints (set X-Accel-Buffering: "no" / proxy_buffering off), 2) enable small keepalive chunking from our side (flush every 128 bytes) as temporary mitigation.
rajesh: For guidance, send them an nginx snippet if they're using nginx or IIS config. Example nginx patch we use in support:```location /v1/stream { proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_set_header Connection ""; proxy_buffering off; chunked_transfer_encoding on; proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $remote_addr; }```
sophie: For IIS there's a known setting to disable response buffering in ARR/proxy. Also recommend enabling a lightweight heartbeat payload like `:heartbeat\n\n` every 15s so WebView doesn't treat connection as stalled.
maria: I'll forward the nginx snippet and ask them to try disabling buffering + send us a new log with req_0a9b3f. Any quick SDK toggles?
tim: We can flip the stream mode flag server-side for their tenant to more frequent flushes. I'll open a quick assist patch. If they prefer client changes, suggest updating WebView to recent Chromium if possible and handle incremental chunks (don't assume each SSE event is a full JSON—append until double newline then parse).
rajesh: Also check for 429/retry headers — if gateway is rate-limiting it can close mid-stream. Look for `HTTP/1.1 429` or `Retry-After` in logs.
maria: Thanks. Customer will try disabling buffering and enable heartbeat. Scheduling a re-test at 2pm PT. I'll post results here. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: assist-ticket created: #POC-4782, assigned to tim and rajesh. Link: https://redwood.support/tickets/POC-4782
maria: Update (2pm PT): customer disabled buffering and we saw continuous SSE without truncation during a 10-minute test. WebView still shows occasional tiny parse hiccups; we think remaining issues are partial-UTF8 on older Chromium — follow-up planned with client devs. Closing triage for now; great work team! :tada:
